About The Job

A problem isn’t truly solved until it’s solved for all. That’s why Googlers build products that help create opportunities for everyone, whether down the street or across the globe. As a Program Manager at Google, you’ll lead complex, multi-disciplinary projects from start to finish — working with stakeholders to plan requirements, manage project schedules, identify risks, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company. Your projects will often span offices, time zones, and hemispheres. It's your job to coordinate the players and keep them up to date on progress and deadlines.

The Global Infrastructure and Energy organization is responsible to deliver the infrastructure to host and connect every machine and every user on the internet, with carbon free energy (CFE). As part of the Commercial Operations arm within the Global Operations for Assets and Tooling team, we are responsible to help the strategic negotiators land agreements quickly and be able to maximize our returns.

The AI and Infrastructure team is redefining what’s possible. We empower Google customers with breakthrough capabilities and insights by delivering AI and Infrastructure at unparalleled scale, efficiency, reliability and velocity. Our customers include Googlers, Google Cloud customers, and billions of Google users worldwide.

We're the driving force behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our cutting-edge AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future. From software to hardware our teams are shaping the future of world-leading hyperscale computing, with key teams working on the development of our TPUs, Vertex AI for Google Cloud, Google Global Networking, Data Center operations, systems research, and much more.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $159000 - $230000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

Responsibilities

Learn more about benefits at Google .

Analyze and report unit costs associated with network acquisition agreements to inform leadership business strategy and equip negotiators for future discussions.
Track utilization of approved budgets against contract execution, and prepare the essential data for regular leadership reporting.
Collaborate closely with regional teams to ensure accurate entry of key agreement terms, project details, and forecasts into required tools, confirming adherence to established processes.
Liaise with central program manager to implement changes in the region, driving awareness and adoption.
Apply AI to automate processes and perform complex analyses.

Marketing Statement

Lincoln Medical and Mental Health Center is one of New York City’s premier acute care hospitals. Located in Downtown Bronx, Lincoln is a teaching hospital renowned for its Centers of Excellence, and a recognized industry leader in the implementation of state-of-the art medical technology and best practices. Our team of highly trained and caring medical professionals is dedicated to providing the highest quality health care that is safe, compassionate, culturally competent and patient-centered. Comprehensive services are offered in three major primary care areas: Medicine, Pediatrics, and Women’s Health in addition to more than eighty (80) specialty services. At NYC Health + Hospitals, our mission is to deliver high quality care health services, without exception. Every employee takes a person-centered approach that exemplifies the ICARE values (Integrity, Compassion, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence) through empathic communication and partnerships between all persons.

Duties & Responsibilities

Purpose of Position
:

This class of positions encompasses professional, supervisory or administrative work of varying degrees of difficulty and responsibility in the operation of a social work department providing psychosocial and other social work services to different types of patients across various settings. All personnel perform related work.

Under general supervision, with some latitude for the exercise of independent judgment, performs the following:

Screens charts for historical and clinical information, conducts psychosocial evaluations through interviews with patients and/or identified surrogates and formulates appropriate social work treatment plans.

May assist in the provision of clinical services only under supervision of a New York State LCSW, licensed psychologist, or psychiatrist.
Performs other related duties, as directed and with required supervision.

Mentors and assists less experienced social work staff in social work techniques and serves as a resource in various aspects of advanced social work practice.

jobs.title: Aboriginal Case Manager – Homes First Program
jobs.description:
Junction Support Services was established with one goal in mind, to support vulnerable people in our community.

Every day, our people work alongside children, young people, individuals and families, empowering brighter futures and building strong, thriving communities together.

About The Role

As the Homes First Aboriginal Case Manager at Junction Support, you will provide culturally safe, trauma-informed, strengths-based and person-centred case management, ensuring Aboriginal clients have choice, voice and control in the support they receive.

You will work alongside clients to identify their goals, strengths and support needs, develop individualised support plans and provide practical assistance to overcome barriers to housing stability. You will also support clients to strengthen connections with culture, Country and community, and build meaningful pathways towards social and emotional wellbeing.

This role is about much more than housing. It is about building trust, walking alongside people, supporting self determination and creating opportunities for Aboriginal people and families to thrive.

This is a full-time maximum-term contract opportunity until 30 June 2029, based at our Wangaratta location.

What You Can Expect

In the role, you will:

Support Aboriginal clients to secure, establish and maintain safe, stable and sustainable tenancies through flexible, person-centred case management.
Embed Housing First, culturally safe, trauma-informed, strengths-based and self-determined practice across all aspects of service delivery.
Develop and review individualised support plans that address housing, wellbeing, family, parenting and practical living needs.
Support connection to culture, Country and community, including building strong partnerships with Aboriginal Community Controlled Organisations and local Aboriginal communities.
Advocate for clients and facilitate connections with health, wellbeing and community services, while proactively identifying and responding to risks that may impact housing stability.
Maintain accurate case records and reporting, participate in multidisciplinary collaboration, supervision and professional development, and contribute to effective transition and exit planning.

About You

You will bring:

Identification as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander.
Relevant qualifications in Community Services, Social Work, Welfare, Behavioural Science or a related field, and/or relevant experience.
Experience working with Aboriginal children, young people, families and/or communities.
Strong understanding of issues affecting Aboriginal communities and experience delivering culturally safe, trauma-informed and strengths-based support.
Demonstrated case management skills, including assessment, support planning, advocacy and client led goal setting.
Understanding of homelessness and Housing First principles, with strong communication, collaboration and relationship-building skills.
Knowledge of family violence information sharing requirements, including FVISS, CISS and MARAM, or willingness to develop this knowledge.

About Us

Junction Support Services is an award-winning regional not-for-profit that has been empowering brighter futures for more than 35 years. We deliver trauma-informed housing, health, disability, education and family services across regional Victoria and NSW, supporting more than 2,500 people each year.

What We Offer

This role offers the opportunity to create meaningful change in your community. Join a team that values connection, growth and making a positive impact in people’s lives.

Why Join Junction?

Increase your take home pay with a generous salary packaging
Enjoy 5 weeks annual leave with 17.5% leave loading on 4 of those weeks
Ongoing professional development
Clinical supervision and debriefing opportunities
Access to agency vehicles for work related travel
Supportive and inclusive team culture
Make a genuine difference every day

How To Apply.

To apply, please click 'Apply'
and submit:

Your current resume, outlining your relevant skills, qualifications, and experience.
A cover letter explaining why you are well suited to this role.
A response to the key selection criteria, demonstrating how your skills, experience, and achievements align with the requirements of the position.

Applications close: 4th October, 2026.

We look forward to receiving your application.

If you have any questions about this opportunity, please contact the People & Culture team on (02) 6043 7400
.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Child Safety

Junction Support Services is a child-safe organisation and an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from First Nations peoples, individuals with disability or lived experience of disability, and people of all cultural backgrounds, gender identities and sexual orientations. We value the unique perspectives and contributions that diversity brings to our workplace and the communities we serve.
